identity.name: German federal government 2024-2025 (composite: finance ministry BMF + economy ministry BMWK)

goals.goal: BMF: convert the frozen Magdeburg earmark into consolidation headroom
BMF: avoid any obligation that outlives Intel's willingness to build
BMWK: retain a German leading-edge logic fab and its supplier ring
BMWK: preserve the credibility of the German subsidy instrument
Cabinet: avoid a public admission that the flagship industrial project failed

fears: BMF: a legally binding, non-unwindable commitment sitting in a narrowed off-budget vehicle
BMF: a supplementary budget or a second budget hole
BMWK: Magdeburg read internationally as a bluff, repricing future German commitments
BMWK: loss of the only leading-edge logic anchor in the domestic ecosystem

factions.name: Finance ministry (BMF)
factions.goal: Budget consolidation; protect the debt brake; reclaim earmarked funds
factions.veto_scope: no federal euro leaves without its budget title

factions.name: Economy ministry (BMWK)
factions.goal: Industrial policy; keep the chip subsidy programme and its industrial line intact
factions.veto_scope: can refuse to sign a reallocation out of its line

factions.name: Chancellery
factions.goal: Political damage control; keep the coalition intact

decision_rule: No federal euro leaves without BMF's budget title; BMWK can block reallocation out of its line but cannot create headroom. When a frozen project competes with a budget gap, the gap wins unless the Chancellery spends political capital - and in 2024 it did not.

resources.resource: Refusal to re-notify a re-scoped use

constraints.constraint: Aid is approved and sized at about EUR 9.9bn for this site
Aid is project- and site-specific; re-scoping needs fresh Commission notification
Funds sit in a specific off-budget vehicle already narrowed by a constitutional court ruling
Saxony-Anhalt holds its own stake and its own fiscal claim on the site
Intel's stated stop reason was market demand, not subsidy size
Intel's cancellation was driven by insufficient customer commitments

options.action: Hold the EUR 9.9bn earmark and wait for Intel to recommit
De-commit the earmark back into consolidation
Re-scope the aid to another project after a new state-aid notification
Convert the envelope into supplier and design-ecosystem support
Conditional re-confirmation if Intel supplies firm offtake and a date

ruled_out.action: Top up the subsidy to make Magdeburg viable
ruled_out.reason: No fiscal room after the budget hole, and it answers a demand problem with money

ruled_out.action: Take an equity stake in the fab
ruled_out.reason: No mandate; Intel did not ask for one

ruled_out.action: Compel Intel to build on the original timetable
ruled_out.reason: A grant is not a supply contract; no performance instrument exists

reaction_function.if: Intel firms a date backed by named customer offtake
reaction_function.then: BMF and BMWK jointly re-confirm the aid, with BMF re-papering the guarantee so it is unwindable
reaction_function.because: BMF will not repeat the original open-ended commitment

reaction_function.if: Intel repeats a delay without new commitments
reaction_function.then: BMF treats it as cancellation and moves to de-commit; BMWK pivots to supplier support
reaction_function.because: The gap wins over the programme

reaction_function.then: The federal share is reduced and the project is kept alive at lower federal cost
BMF books the EUR 9.9bn as available headroom; BMWK absorbs the credibility loss without a replacement anchor
reaction_function.because: No substitute anchor is available in the window

beliefs_about.belief: Intel's binding constraint is customer commitments and capex discipline, not German subsidy size
Intel will let the Magdeburg option lapse and attribute it to demand rather than to the money
Intel assumes Berlin will park the money rather than admit the flagship failed - a belief FACT-004 contradicts

falsifiers: BMF voluntarily re-earmarks or increases the EUR 9.9bn for Magdeburg after the cancellation
Evidence that the aid was already disbursed and legally irreversible before the 2024 pause
BMWK accepts the claw-back without contest, showing the internal split is weaker than modelled
premises_missing: Whether any of the EUR 9.9bn was disbursed before the 2024 pause or only committed
Repayment and claw-back terms of the Commission's aid decision
Size and conditionality of Saxony-Anhalt's co-funding offer
The post-February-2025 federal government's position on the earmark
